source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CloudHQ MCC1 publishes one hard number: 2,232,875 square feet of technical space in Prince William County, Virginia. That figure places the campus among the largest footprints in a state already dense with data center infrastructure. No IT load in megawatts, no critical power figure, and no redundancy tier are published on the operator's spec page, so no power-based estimate of rack or accelerator capacity can be responsibly made here.

Without a published megawatt figure, this site cannot rank MCC1 among the 19 Virginia facilities that do publish capacity. Those 19 facilities together account for 1,326 MW of published IT load across 326 mapped facilities statewide, and MCC1 is not among them. Whether its actual power draw is large or small relative to that pool is not determinable from what the operator has released.

For a reader evaluating AI relevance, the square footage signals that the physical shell exists at scale, but shell space alone does not confirm power delivery, cooling infrastructure, or network density, all of which determine whether a building can support high-density GPU training or inference workloads. No certifications are listed in the published specifications. Until CloudHQ publishes a critical IT load figure, MCC1 remains a large building whose AI hosting capacity is unknown.
